text:
Priya: quick flag-up: the new per-model mini-card in the console is showing 'cache savings' that look bigger than the model cost line for some routes. saw this in tenant Z during a spike.
Omar: can you screenshot or paste the numbers? is this on the 24h view or billing (7d) view?
Priya: 24h view. example: model 'redwood-lite' cost $0.32 but cache_savings $0.41 (card shows net -$0.09).
Jen: ugh. did we accidentally apply amortized 7d credits into the 24h panel? the rollup job has both windows but console might be picking the wrong field.
Alex: I pulled the backend row: token_cost_24h=0.32, cache_credit_7d_amortized=2.87, cache_credit_24h=0.41, sample_coverage=12%. So console is showing cache_credit_24h raw. That's legitimately > cost in the sampled data.
Priya: so it's not a bug in field mapping, it's a sampling / attribution issue where cache credits accrue across sessions. we need to make this less alarming in the UI.
Omar: telemetry detail: cache-crediting uses span-level attribution and sometimes attributes a full cache amortization to a single route even if tokens were recorded under sibling routes due to trace sampling. That explains overcrediting on low coverage cells.
Jen: proposal: in the console, for exploration panels show a cleaned metric "estimated cache savings" = MIN(cache_credit_24h, token_cost_24h) and display a confidence pill derived from sample_coverage. For billing panels, show the canonical billing basis (7d amortized) with a clear label.
Alex: backend needs to emit both windows plus sample_count so console can compute. we already have sample_coverage pct but sample_count helps for thresholds.
Priya: +1. also add an info icon with microcopy: "Estimated: based on sampled telemetry; may exceed observed cost when coverage is low."
Omar: implementation tasks: (1) econ-rollup add fields: cache_credit_24h, cache_credit_7d_amortized, sample_count (RED-ENG-3010), (2) console compute displayed_savings behind feature flag (RED-ENG-3011), (3) add confidence pill logic: low <25, med 25-75, high >75 (RED-ENG-3012).
Jen: should the clamp happen in backend or UI? If multiple consumers need the same behavior (alerts, reports) maybe backend should offer a clamped_display_savings as well.
Alex: I prefer UI compute for flexibility; backend can offer a recommended_clamp boolean and provenance fields. but for billing APIs backend must be authoritative.
Priya: sounds reasonable. we'll version the rollup schema (v2) so billing consumers still read canonical fields. console will use clamped view by default but allow toggle to show raw numbers.
Omar: also add an alert rule: when cache_credit_24h > token_cost_24h by >50% and sample_coverage <30% create an ops ticket for investigation. non-billing signal.
infra-bot: Created tasks: RED-ENG-3010, RED-ENG-3011, RED-ENG-3012.
Jen: UX copy draft: "Estimated cache savings (clamped). Values are based on sampled telemetry; click for confidence and amortization basis."
Priya: fine. let's also include a small dotted-line tooltip that links to docs about sampling and amortization.
Alex: I'll start the rollup PR — emit both windows and sample_count, bump schema. Jen can land console changes behind flag. Omar will add the alert rule.
Priya: timeline: rollup PR -> test schema in staging -> console behind flag -> canary 10 tenants 48h -> enable.
Omar: will add unit tests for the clamp and confidence computation.
Jen: I'll mock low-coverage scenarios for QA.
Priya: thanks team. syncing tomorrow 10:30 to check canary metrics.
Alex: noted.
infra-bot: Deploy pipeline queued for RED-ENG-3010 (env=staging).
